What Is The Only Four Letter Word You Won’t Hear
In DEAland’s Largest Movie Theater Chain?
H-E-M-P!

January 18, 1999
From Heather H. Lentz, Owner
THE CHANGE
cchange@bellsouth.net  (TheChange)
Spartanburg, SC.

To all concerned parties:

My name is Heather Lentz and I own a hemp related store in Spartanburg, SC.

As the mother of a 3-year old, I am very concerned about the state of our environment. I am a firm believer in HEMP and ALL aspects that it has to offer to our planet. I am very disgruntled at the common ignorant attitude towards the wealth this plant has to offer us. I feel that it is a very important task that those of us who are aware, educate all those who are not.

Owning a store of this nature in this region of the country is not always an easy task and it is very disheartening to find people who are unwilling to support our plight.

Therefore, it is of utmost importance that those of us who do share common interest in the HEMP field support each other, ban together, and stamp out ignorance. Some of the people who are receiving this email I have had contact with before, some I have not, but I know that you are all working on this enormous task of informing.

Hence, I feel it very necessary to share the following information.

Recently, a corporate representative of Carmike Corporation (a very large movie corporation) contacted me in regards to advertising locally in their monthly new film release magazine. The representative told me that she noticed another ad of ours and thought that we would benefit from reaching their movie audience.

I received the usual sales pitch and then was told there would be one slight catch.

Although she "personally had no problem with it," she informed me that we would not be allowed to use the word "HEMP" or any such reference. She stated that it was Carmike Corporate policy and such stores are actually on a "Do Not Contact List" but she thought since we sell numerous other items, we could simple feature those items and leave out the "unwanted."

I then informed her that although her offer probably would bring great recognition to our business, HEMP is a very important subject to me and if her company could not support ALL aspects of our business, especially the most important one, I simply could not contribute to supporting the company she represents.

When I first began drafting this letter to you, I did not know how large this corporation was or the regions in which it spanned. I simply believed that everyone who had a movie theater in their area which is owned by Carmike should be made aware of their intolerance so that the public may try to either help change Carmike’s corporate policy or make the decision not to support such asinine intolerance.

However, with each passing minute, my rage towards their policy grows and while working on this letter, I decided to search for more info on the corporation itself. Frighteningly enough, by visiting their web site (www.carmike.com) I discovered that they claim to be "the largest motion picture exhibitor in the United States, operating 513 theaters with aggregate of 2,703 screens in markets located in 36 states."

WHEW...what power and money they must hold....and they have actually "black balled" hemp stores and companies? Now this definately sounds like info that consumers need to be made aware of. I hope that I have provided you with something to investigate and if you deem it so...please use your various avenues of media to spread the news!!!!!

Thank you for your attention.

Heather H. Lentz, Owner
THE CHANGE
